hints: Look carefully at each diagram and count every charged group: each COO- or O- counts as -1 and each N+H3 counts as +1.
Add the plus and minus charges for each amino acid to get its net charge. Remember a zwitterion with one +1 and one -1 has an overall charge of zero.
walkthrough:
**Identify the charged groups**

Each amino acid in water exists as an ion. The carboxyl group shown as COO- carries a -1 charge, and the amino group shown as N+H3 carries a +1 charge. Side chains (R groups) can add extra charges.

**Add up charges for glycine and alanine**

For glycine: one COO- ($-1$) + one N+H3 ($+1$) = 0. For alanine: one COO- ($-1$) + one N+H3 ($+1$) = 0.

$$-1 + 1 = 0$$
So both are neutral zwitterions with no overall charge.

**Add up charges for lysine and aspartate**

For lysine: side chain H3N+ ($+1$) + COO- ($-1$) + N+H3 ($+1$) = +1 overall. For aspartate: side chain COO- ($-1$) + COO- ($-1$) + N+H3 ($+1$) = -1 overall.

$$+1 -1 +1 = +1 \text{ for lysine}$$
$$-1 -1 +1 = -1 \text{ for aspartate}$$
So these two do have an overall non-zero charge, which gives answer C.

options.A: Alanine is neutral (one -1 and one +1 cancel to zero), so it does not have an overall charge.
options.B: Both alanine and glycine are neutral zwitterions with charges that cancel to zero.
options.C: Correct. Lysine has a net +1 charge and aspartate has a net -1 charge, so both have an overall charge.
options.D: Glycine is neutral (one -1 and one +1 cancel to zero), so it does not have an overall charge.
